title: London's St Paul's ~$35. Shanghai's Jing'an Temple ~$7 | China Travel Expert
description:
Two famous city landmarks you pay to walk into — and the price gap is wild.

St Paul's Cathedral in London charges £27 for an adult sightseeing ticket (about $35). Shanghai's golden Jing'an Temple charges ¥50 — about $7. Same kind of awe, one-fifth the price. Which one do you walk into?

Jing'an Temple (静安寺) is one of Shanghai's oldest. It was founded back in 247 CE, took the name Jing'an ('tranquillity and peace') in 1008, and has stood on this spot — now the heart of the city's luxury-mall district on West Nanjing Road — since 1216. Note the honest part: the gilded halls you see today are modern reconstructions (the temple was rebuilt in 1983 and the Jing'an Pagoda finished in 2010), so this is about the site and the ticket, not an 800-year-old building.

🧭 Expert Tip: go late afternoon for the golden light on the roofs, and you can pair it with a free walk through the Jing'an district — the contrast of incense smoke and designer flagship stores is the whole point.

伦敦圣保罗大教堂门票约35美元；上海静安寺门票50元，约7美元，差不多五分之一的价钱。静安寺始建于247年，1216年迁到今址，如今被奢侈品商场环绕——不过你看到的金顶大殿是现代重建的（1983年重修，静安宝塔2010年落成）。
